Acquisition.description: A modality-agnostic protocol used to acquire neuroimaging or associated physiological data, holding only what every modality has in common. One Acquisition carries one modality: simultaneous recordings such as EEG+fMRI are separate Acquisition records that a Task lists together. Everything modality-specific lives in the class the Modality value instantiates -- MRI, EEG, FNIRS, PET, or OtherModality.

acquisition_duration_seconds.description: Total usable acquisition or recording duration in seconds. Useful for filtering studies by the amount of data contributing to an analysis, especially resting-state and continuous recordings.

acquisition_type.description: The concrete subclass this record instantiates. Derived by the mapper from the modality value's `instantiates`, never extracted.

brain_coverage.description:
How much of the brain the acquired volume contained. This is the extent the SCANNER sampled, and it is a third axis distinct from the two the schema already carries: `Analysis.spatial_scope` is what the analysis tested, and `InferenceSettings.correction_scope` with `search_volume` is where multiple comparisons were controlled. A voxelwise analysis over a volume that clipped the cerebellum is `whole_brain` in scope and `partial` here, and an ROI analysis of a whole-head acquisition is the reverse. Never infer this from either of those.
It describes the volume behind the REPORTED results. A scan that clipped a structure in participants who were then excluded is `whole_brain`, because the analysed volume was not clipped; calling it `partial` would say the opposite of what the results rest on.
A field of view or slice prescription in millimetres is not by itself a statement of coverage. Where only the geometry is given, the value is an inference and `value_source` records it as one. Which structure a partial volume missed is not a field of its own -- the evidence span carries that detail.

device.description: The scanner, amplifier, or recording system this acquisition was made on, by identifier. Acquisitions made on one machine reference one record; a second record asserts the study used a second machine.

modality.description:
Imaging or recording modality. A value in the Modality vocabulary also names the class holding this acquisition's modality-specific parameters, through that value's `instantiates`.
Open vocabulary: write the source's own wording in the field when nothing here fits, because the value is required and a closed range would discard the whole acquisition over one unrecognised word. Only a vocabulary value carries an `instantiates`, so an acquisition outside it resolves to the base class until normalization maps the wording back on -- which is why `acquisition_type` is derived rather than extracted, and why an unmapped modality is worth reporting.

Acquisition.title: Acquisition

AgeUnit.description: The unit the age summaries are in, folded from the source's wording. Closed, because the point of the field is that two studies' ages are comparable, and an open range would put that back where it started.
AgeUnit.title: AgeUnit

Allocation.description: How participants came to be in the arm they were in. Open vocabulary: write the source's own wording in the field when nothing here fits.
Allocation.title: Allocation

Analysis.description:
A distinct reported inferential map or tested effect, linking its source acquisitions, sample, paradigm context, tested effect, preprocessing, model estimation, inference settings, and source result tables.
Create one Analysis for each distinct tested effect. Separate Analyses are required when normalized direction, participant-group comparison, method, the pattern of `effect.cells`, seed or connectivity model, decoded variable, component identity, or spatial_scope differ, and when an omnibus effect and its directional post-hoc contrast are both reported. ROI definitions, acquisition summaries, descriptive sample tables, and masks without inferential effects are not Analyses. Nor is a map reported with no inferential test at all -- an ICA or PCA component map presented descriptively, a connectivity matrix given without a test -- there being nothing for such a map to be the effect of.

acquisitions.description: Acquisition protocols supplying data to this analysis. Structural, diffusion, and other non-paradigm analyses are linked directly through this field.

assessments.description: Assessments whose measurements were used in or selected the sample for this analysis.

coordinate_space.description:
Coordinate reference space or template the spatial results are reported in, such as MNI152 or Talairach. **The authoritative of the two places this can live**: where this and a `Table.coordinate_space` disagree, this one is the analysis's space, since a table can be parsed as one space while the analysis it reports states another.
Both may be filled, and usually are: the table parser fills the tables and the same parse supplies this when every table behind the analysis agrees, leaving the model to answer only where they do not. Never inferred from the model's `spatial_unit` -- an analysis on a surface reports a surface template.

defines_regions.description: Regions this analysis produced: a localizer's clusters, or peaks of a contrast later used as seeds or ROIs. Populated on the analysis a region came *from*, not on those that use it, so a region whose `definition_method` is `same_study_analysis` and which another analysis lists in `regions` or `seed_regions` is a circularity the record states rather than asserts.

definition.description: Precise statement of the tested effect in the source's own words, minimally cleaned. Always source-grounded. For an interaction it must state the direction of the interaction as the source states it; for an ordered contrast it must keep the ordering that the cell directions cannot express.

details.description: The method that produced the map and its method-specific payload. The populated subclass identifies the method. A voxelwise, vertexwise, or ROI-wise GLM, mixed-effects model, ANOVA, ANCOVA, or robust regression takes MassUnivariateDetails; a method outside the first-class families takes OtherAnalysisDetails and names itself in method_label.

effect.description: What was tested about the map. Universal across every method.

groups.description: The participant cohorts the analysis ran on, and how many participants each contributed. Membership only: this slot says which people were analysed, never what was compared. A cohort comparison is a pair of directional `Cell`s on the model term whose levels name the cohorts, exactly as a condition or occasion comparison is.

inference_settings.description: The thresholding and correction this analysis was reported under, by identifier. Analyses sharing one scheme reference one record; an analysis thresholded or corrected differently takes its own. Not the model's -- one fit thresholded two ways is two records here and one `model_estimation`. A contrast reported at two search volumes is two analyses sharing one `model_estimation`, not one analysis with the stricter threshold.

interpretations.description: The source's own statement of what this analysis found and what it means, typically in Results and Discussion, verbatim or minimally cleaned. Always source-grounded, and the counterpart of `definition`: that field is the Methods-side statement of what was tested, this one is the Results/Discussion-side statement of what came of it.

measure.description: The scientific quantity of the map, by identifier, independent of the statistic used to test it. Analyses of one quantity reference one record; an analysis of a different quantity takes its own. Required: a paper vague about what it measured still takes a record, with `source_label` as given and `extraction_status: not_reported` elsewhere.

mirror_of.description:
Present only on an analysis the builder derived by reversing another one, and naming the analysis it reverses.
A results table with both signs in one column reports one contrast read two ways. The paper's prose describes one direction, so only that half is extracted and the other is rebuilt arithmetically -- same cells, directions flipped. This slot is what says so. Without it the two halves look like independent findings, and a meta-analysis that counts both counts one sample twice.

model_estimation.description: The model this analysis's contrast was taken from: its family, estimator, stage, software, and the terms it was specified with. What was selected out of those terms is `effect`. Required: a paper that describes a contrast and never names an estimator still takes a record, with the terms it does state and `extraction_status: not_reported` elsewhere. Analyses sharing one design reference one record; an analysis specified or estimated differently takes its own.

model_representation_notes.description: Model components that could not be represented or were represented only approximately, for an analysis whose method is otherwise first-class. Examples include random slopes, latent variables, dynamic connectivity, and dependencies between terms. An analysis whose method has no stable structured decomposition at all takes NotStructurableDetails instead.

name.description: Study-local label for the analysis or inferential result, in the source's words.

outcome.description: Whether anything survived the threshold this analysis was tested at: a cluster, a peak, a significant region. The answer to "did this contrast find anything", which `Effect.cells` cannot give -- a cell's direction is the sign of the contrast that was tested, and is written the same whether the test found an effect or not. Meta-analyses exclude null effects and pool only analyses that reported foci, so a tested-and-null contrast and a reported effect must not extract to the same record. Applies only to an analysis whose coordinate set is a `result` (or has no role yet): an ROI, seed, reference or display set was not tested here, so it has no outcome.

prespecification.description:
Whether this contrast was planned before the data were seen or arrived at afterwards.
Open vocabulary: write the source's own wording in the field when neither value fits. The two are not a spectrum and the words a source uses for them are many -- `post-hoc`, `confirmatory`, `planned`, `hypothesis-driven` -- so a closed range would discard the whole analysis over a synonym. Normalization maps the wording onto the two values.

regions.description:
The regions the analysis ran over -- its search space, what `spatial_scope: roi` restricts it to. Empty for whole-brain and searchlight, where the emptiness asserts that inference was not restricted.
Not the analysis's seeds: a whole-brain seed-based analysis has a seed and no search-space region, so putting one here says the opposite of what it did. Seeds are `ConnectivityDetails.seed_regions`.

source_table_analysis.description:
The key of the coordinate-parse analysis this analysis's results were read from: `ParsedAnalysis.key` in neuroimaging-paper-parse, `<table id>#<h>` for a table's row group or `text#<h>` for coordinates read from the text, where `h` hashes the cells or character spans its points came from. Derived from cells, not position, so a re-parse that groups the same cells reaches the same key. When pondie revised the parse, the key is the revision's.
This schema stores no coordinates, so reaching an analysis's foci means joining through the parse, and `tables` alone cannot do it: a table usually reports several contrasts and several analyses usually cite the same table. This key is what makes the join exact.
Copy it from the bracketed key the stage-1 listing prints beside each parsed analysis. One key and not a list, because one analysis is read from one row group; an analysis whose results span two tables cites both in `tables` and names here the row group that defined it.

spatial_scope.description: Spatial domain of the analysis modelled. The spatial_scope refers to what voxels were modelled, not which voxels/brain regions had a correction applied.

statistical_maps.description: Statistical maps made available for this analysis.

tables.description: The source tables reporting results for this analysis.

tasks.description:
The participant paradigms that contextualize this analysis. An analysis can span paradigms, as a cross-task conjunction or a localizer-plus-main-task analysis does.
A resting-state analysis names its Task here like any other: the resting-state protocol is a paradigm, and a Task record exists for it. What leaves this empty is an analysis with no paradigm at all -- morphometry, diffusion, a static PET scan -- which is linked through `acquisitions` instead.

Analysis.title: Analysis

AnalysisDetails.description: Base class for the method-specific payload of one Analysis, instantiated only through its subclasses. Analysis.details is required, so exactly one subclass always applies.

details_type.description: The concrete details subclass carried by this payload. Populated from the class itself, not extracted.

AnalysisDetails.title: AnalysisDetails

AnalysisGroup.description: One participant cohort the analysis ran on, and how many of its participants it included. Membership and sample size only. A comparison *between* cohorts is a pair of directional `Cell`s on the term whose levels name them.

group.description: The cohort this entry refers to, by identifier. The cohort's own properties are on the Group record.

n.description: Number of participants from this cohort included in this analysis. This is where a cohort's analysed size lives -- Group carries the recruitment funnel down to acquisition and nothing past it -- so populate it whenever the source gives a number, and expect it to be smaller than the acquired count when an analysis drops participants for motion or missing data.

AnalysisGroup.title: AnalysisGroup

AnalysisOutcome.description: Whether the tested effect produced any finding at the threshold the source applied. Closed: the two are the only answers, and a source that does not say takes `not_reported` rather than a third value.
AnalysisOutcome.title: AnalysisOutcome

AnalysisType.description: The method that produced the statistical map, independent of what was tested about it. A between-group comparison of connectivity, decoding accuracy, or component loadings keeps the method here and records the comparison in Effect. Bound only by ConjunctionComponent.analysis_type; an Analysis states its method by which AnalysisDetails subclass it fills. Open vocabulary: write the source's own wording in the field when nothing here fits.
AnalysisType.title: AnalysisType

AnchorKind.description: What an `anchor` coordinate set defines. Open vocabulary.
AnchorKind.title: AnchorKind

Arm.description: One thing participants were assigned to receive, or to receive in place of it.

agent.description: The drug, agent, or stimulation target this arm received, as the source names it. The name only; dose, unit, route, and schedule are not recorded.

arm_kind.description: What class of thing this arm received. Required, so an arm whose kind the source leaves unclear still carries the slot, as `extraction_status: not_reported`.

description.description: Complete definition of what this arm received.

name.description: Short arm label as the source states it, for example methylphenidate, sham tDCS, waitlist.

Arm.title: Arm

ArmKind.description: What class of thing an arm received. Spans both the manipulation and the thing it was compared against, both being arms here: a drug against an active comparator is a different comparison from a drug against a placebo, so the two take different values. Open vocabulary: write the source's own wording in the field when nothing here fits.
ArmKind.title: ArmKind

Assessment.description: A behavioral, cognitive, biological, clinical, or questionnaire-based instrument or procedure that produces participant-level measurements independently of the neuroimaging acquisition or experimental conditions.

assessment_type.description: Broad type, such as cognitive test, clinical scale, diagnostic interview, questionnaire, behavioral task, physiological measure, or a biospecimen assay such as salivary cortisol or a plasma marker. Free text rather than a vocabulary: create a category if none of these fit.

description.description: Description of the assessment and the measurements it produced, including the purpose the source gives for administering it -- establishing a group's diagnosis, screening a comorbidity, grading severity, characterizing everyone. That purpose is what decides whether a group may name this assessment as its `diagnostic_instrument`, and it is often the only sentence distinguishing the two.

name.description: Name of the assessment, such as Digit Span, MMSE, or BDI.

Assessment.title: Assessment

AssignmentStructure.description:
How the cohorts a study compares came about. Open vocabulary: write the source's own wording in the field when nothing here fits.
**The first question is whether there are arms at all.** Two cohorts are in parallel in the ordinary sense of the word, so a study that assigned nobody to anything reads as `parallel` on the plain meaning and is wrong. `observational_cohorts` is the value for it, and it has no arms.
AssignmentStructure.title: AssignmentStructure

Blinding.description: Who was kept unaware of the assignment. Open vocabulary: write the source's own wording in the field when nothing here fits.
Blinding.title: Blinding

BrainCoverage.description: Extent of the brain contained in an acquired volume. Two values, because the useful question downstream is binary -- could a focus have been reported from anywhere in the brain, or not -- and the structures a partial volume missed vary too much to enumerate.
BrainCoverage.title: BrainCoverage

CategoryDistribution.description: One category in an aggregate participant distribution. Labels are free text, kept in the study's own terminology. At least one of count or percentage should be supplied when the source reports a quantitative distribution.

category.description: The distribution bucket counted by this entry, labelled as the study writes it and not normalized to any external scheme: `female`, `left-handed`, `Hispanic or Latino`.

category_normalized.description:
`category` folded onto the answer set for the distribution this entry belongs to. **Derived, not extracted**: `pondie.normalization.sex_distribution` and `pondie.normalization.handedness_distribution` set it, and `category` keeps the study's own wording.
The answer set depends on the slot, which is why the range is open here rather than an enum: sex folds to MALE/FEMALE/OTHER/UNKNOWN, handedness to RIGHT/LEFT/AMBIDEXTROUS/OTHER/UNKNOWN. A distribution with no normalizer -- gender, race, ethnicity -- leaves this unset rather than guessing.
Unset is not UNKNOWN. UNKNOWN says a normalizer read the wording and could not place it, which is a wording worth a rule; unset says none ran.

count.description: Number of participants assigned to this category.

denominator.description: Number of participants used as the denominator for the percentage.

percentage.description: Percentage of the relevant group in this category.

reporting_framework.description: The classification system the study used for these categories, in its own words, such as the OMB or NIH race and ethnicity categories, a named handedness inventory, or a self-report question's answer set.

CategoryDistribution.title: CategoryDistribution

Cell.description:
One side of the tested comparison: a level of a model term, and which way that level entered. The unit a contrast is built from.
A cell points at a `ModelTerm`. The term's `FactorLevel`s record which cohort, condition, occasion, or arm carries each level. Joining through the model recovers the contrast's entities, including its conditions and cohorts. The `term` is the comparison axis: cells sharing a term compare within a factor, cells on different terms compare across them.
A cell over a term that declares no levels -- a slope, or a product column -- leaves `level` unset and carries its `direction` alone.

direction.description:
How this cell entered the contrast: the weight's sign for a categorical level, the fitted coefficient's sign for a continuous term, or the interaction coefficient's sign for a product column -- read as the named level's slope relative to the others when the cell names one (`level`).
Signs, never numeric weights. For an ordered comparison mark the extremes `positive` and `negative`, leave the levels in between out of `cells` -- absence is the zero weight -- and keep the ordering on `FactorLevel.order`.

label.description: The source's wording for this level in this comparison, when it differs from the level's own label on the model.

level.description:
The level represented by this cell, matching a `FactorLevel.level` on the referenced ModelTerm. The model states the level vocabulary; this field only identifies the level placed on this side of the comparison.
Required exactly when the referenced term declares levels. A slope declares none, and its cell names none. A product column declares none either, but a signed cell on one crossing a factor with a continuous term may name a level of the factor: the cohort or condition whose slope has the cell's sign, relative to the factor's other levels. "Maltreatment was negatively associated with rACC activation in the PTSD group, but not in controls" is `direction: negative` with `level: PTSD group`. Without the level the sign has no reference, since which level the difference is taken from is a coding choice.

term.description: The model term this cell belongs to, by identifier. It must be one of the terms of the ModelEstimation the containing Analysis references, or of a stage that model reaches through `inputs_from` -- a group contrast of a first-level condition, or of a seed's time series, is a cell on that stage's term rather than on a copy of it.

Cell.title: Cell

Condition.description: A named condition of a task: a modelled state, event type, or baseline that an analysis can contrast against another. Only what happened inside the paradigm -- the occasion the task was run on and the arm it was run under are Timepoints and Arms, and enter an analysis as levels of their own model terms, compared by `Cell`s on the Effect.

condition_kind.description: What kind of state this was: an active task state, a rest or fixation period, or a state the source calls a control or neutral condition. A field of its own rather than a phrase in `description`, which a consumer cannot reliably read it out of.

description.description:
Complete definition of the condition, including whether it put a demand on the participant. Whether it was a rest, fixation, or control state belongs in `condition_kind`.
A rest or fixation period inside another paradigm is a Condition of that paradigm's Task. A standalone resting-state run is not: it is its own Task, with one condition or none. The distinction is which paradigm the participant was in, not what they were doing -- a fixation baseline between working-memory blocks belongs to the working-memory Task.
What a tested effect was measured against is not recorded here: a contrast against this condition gives it a `negative` cell, and a contrast against the unmodelled implicit baseline has no second cell.

name.description: Short condition label that distinguishes the condition from other task periods or modeled effects.

stimulus_content.description:
What this condition's stimuli were about -- their category, not the channel (`Task.stimulus_modality`) or the materials (`Task.stimuli`): a cigarette photograph is `cigarettes`. Faces, scenes, words, tones, music, food, money -- examples, not a vocabulary.
Leave unset where the stimulus does not distinguish this condition from the others: every n-back load level shows the same letters.

Condition.title: Condition

ConditionKind.description:
What kind of state a condition was, in itself. Open vocabulary: write the source's own wording in the field when nothing here fits.
Intrinsic to the condition and not its role in any one contrast. What a tested effect was measured against is carried by `Cell.direction`, which a contrast fills for each side; a condition can be the comparator in one analysis and the target in another, and recording that here would make it a property of the wrong thing.
ConditionKind.title: ConditionKind

ConjunctionComponent.description: One component effect of a conjunction, carrying its own direction in its definition.

analysis_id.description: Identifier of the sibling Analysis record for this component, when it is separately reported.

analysis_type.description: The component's own method, when it is known and differs from the others. A method the vocabulary cannot name is written here as free text.

definition.description: Source-grounded statement of the component effect, including its direction.

ConjunctionComponent.title: ConjunctionComponent

ConjunctionDetails.description: Payload for a conjunction. The conjunction's own cells describe the conjoint effect, so its kind derives like any other; what each component was in its own right is on that component's `analysis_type` and `definition`, which is where a conjunction over unlike components records the difference.

components.description: The independently defined effects that were combined.

details_type.description: The concrete details subclass carried by this payload. Populated from the class itself, not extracted.

implementation.description: Procedure that computed the conjunction, recorded separately from the hypothesis it tested.

null_hypothesis.description: Which null hypothesis was tested. Only the conjunction null licenses the strong reading.

ConjunctionDetails.title: ConjunctionDetails

ConjunctionImplementation.description: Procedure used to compute the conjunction, which is not the same statement as the null hypothesis it tested: a minimum-statistic test is the usual implementation of the conjunction null. Open vocabulary: write the source's own wording in the field when nothing here fits.
ConjunctionImplementation.title: ConjunctionImplementation

ConnectivityDetails.description:
Payload for an analysis of a relationship between regions, whether that relationship is estimated from a signal or across subjects. Signal-based connectivity is the common case; structural covariance -- correlating cortical thickness or volume between a seed region and every other, across participants rather than within one -- shares the same shape of answer, so it takes this payload with `structural_covariance` as its method.
Nothing here carries direction. The sign of the connectivity parameter, and whether the experimental effect raised or lowered it, are what the analysis tested, so they are `Effect.cells` like the direction of any other result: a negative PPI is a `negative` cell on the term the coupling was estimated for, and coupling higher in one condition than another is that condition term crossed. A sign recorded here as well would be a second route to one fact, and the two can disagree -- a whole-map `increased` beside a pair of crossed cells says the map has one direction and two at once.

details_type.description: The concrete details subclass carried by this payload. Populated from the class itself, not extracted.

edges.description: Named region pairs, when the source reports specific edges.

inference_target.description: What the statistical test was about: the strength of a connection, which of several models fits better, or a network taken as a whole. A model comparison and a parameter test answer different questions and are not poolable.

modulatory_input.description: Modulatory input of the model, for DCM and related methods.

seed_regions.description: Seed or source regions, by identifier. What each one is and how it was delimited is on the `Region`; naming it here says only that this analysis seeded from it.

target_regions.description: Target regions, by identifier. Empty for a seed-to-whole-brain analysis.

ConnectivityDetails.title: ConnectivityDetails

ConnectivityEdge.description: One reported connection between two named regions.

directionality.description: Whether this edge is genuinely directed. Derived from the containing analysis's `connectivity_method`, which is what decides it: only a directed model supports a claim about which region influences which, and the wording of the paper cannot change that. The mapper's `edge_directionality_from_method` table in extraction-to-storage.map.yaml holds the value per method, and leaves this unset for a method written as free text, there being nothing to derive from.

source_region.description: Source region of the edge, by identifier.

target_region.description: Target region of the edge, by identifier.

ConnectivityEdge.title: ConnectivityEdge

ConnectivityMethod.description: Method used to estimate connectivity. Open vocabulary: write the source's own wording in the field when nothing here fits.
ConnectivityMethod.title: ConnectivityMethod

CoordinateRole.description: What a set of reported coordinates is for. A paper prints coordinates for six reasons, and only the first is a finding; the rest locate something the study used, measured with, quoted, or showed. Open vocabulary: write the source's own wording when nothing here fits.
CoordinateRole.title: CoordinateRole

CoordinateSet.description:
A group of coordinates reported together -- a row group of a table, or a run of sentences in the text -- and what it is for. The coordinates stay in the parse, as for tables; this records their role and links them to what they belong to: the analysis a result reports, the regions an anchor locates.
A set has one role: its dominant one. The groups come from the table parse, which splits a table by what was tested rather than by what each row is for, so a set can mix roles -- a connectivity results table that lists its own seed as a row. Such a set keeps the role of most of its points, and the odd point takes that role with it. This is a known error, about 1.3% of sets, accepted rather than splitting the parse's groups.

analysis.description: For a `result`, the analysis whose findings these are. The same join `Analysis.source_table_analysis` makes from the other side, here for sets read from the text as well.

anchor_kind.description: For an `anchor`, what it defines. Absent for every other role.

description.description: What the set is, in the source's words, when the role alone does not say.

id.description: The key the coordinate parse gave this set, `ParsedAnalysis.key` in neuroimaging-paper-parse: `<table id>#<h>` for a table's row group, the same key `Analysis.source_table_analysis` names, or `text#<h>` for a run of sentences. `h` hashes the cells or character spans the set's points were read from, so the key survives a re-parse that groups the same points.

regions.description: For an `anchor`, the regions these coordinates locate.

result_kind.description: For a `result`, the kind of analysis that produced it. Absent for every other role.

table.description: The table this set was read from. Absent for a set read from the text.

text_excerpt.description: For a set read from the text, the sentences it was read from: the sentence holding the coordinates and its neighbours, extended past any neighbour that also holds coordinates.

CoordinateSet.title: CoordinateSet

DecodingClass.description: One class discriminated by a decoding analysis.

condition.description: The experimental condition this class corresponds to, when it is one.

label.description: The class label as the source names it, such as `faces` or `left hand`.

DecodingClass.title: DecodingClass

DecodingDetails.description: Payload for a classification or pattern-discriminability analysis. Above-chance decoding is one signed cell with nothing crossed, and the reference it beat is `PerformanceMetric.reference_value`, which is per metric because accuracy against chance and AUC against 0.5 are two references. A between-cohort accuracy comparison is a crossed cohort term; accuracy regressed on a behavioural score is a cell on a continuous term. Spatial scope is recorded on the Analysis, including for searchlight analyses.

classes.description: The classes discriminated. These are non-directional: direction, where it exists, is carried by Effect.

decoded_variable.description: The variable the classifier or discriminability test predicted.

details_type.description: The concrete details subclass carried by this payload. Populated from the class itself, not extracted.

generalization.description: Train/test split for cross-decoding, when the analysis generalized across sets.

performance_metrics.description: The performance measures reported for this map, one entry each. Papers routinely give several of the same analysis -- accuracy with sensitivity and specificity, or accuracy with AUC -- and each carries its own value and its own reference. Record every one the source reports.

validation_scheme.description: Cross-validation or resampling scheme, such as leave-one-run-out.

DecodingDetails.title: DecodingDetails

DecompositionMethod.description: The algorithm that produced the components or latent variables, which decides what their values and signs mean. Independent of `second_block`, since one block structure is reachable by several algorithms: a brain-behaviour covariance can be decomposed by PLS or by CCA. Open vocabulary: write the source's own wording in the field when nothing here fits.
DecompositionMethod.title: DecompositionMethod

DesignType.description: How a task's events were modelled in time -- not what the task was or what it showed. Open vocabulary: write the source's own wording in the field when nothing here fits.
DesignType.title: DesignType

Device.description:
The scanner, amplifier, or recording system an acquisition was made on, split into the two parts a source reliably reports. Either part can be missing: papers name a model with no manufacturer as often as the reverse.
One record is one physical machine, referenced by every acquisition made on it: a study that collected functional, structural and diffusion scans in one session has three Acquisitions and one Device. Two records mean the study says it used two machines -- a second site, or a rescan on different hardware -- which is a claim about the data and not a way of recording that two sequences differed.

id.description: Stable identifier used by Acquisition foreign-key references.

manufacturer.description: Company that made the device, as reported, such as Siemens, GE, Philips, Brain Products, or NIRx.

model.description: Model or product name of the device, as reported, such as Prisma, Signa, Achieva, or actiCHamp.

Device.title: Device

Direction.description:
How a term entered or came out of an analysis, using one vocabulary for every term type. Both a categorical level on the plus side of a comparison and a continuous term with a positive coefficient are `positive`. The referenced term's `type` distinguishes them. For a cell over a **product** term, this field gives the interaction coefficient's sign, not either component's slope.
It is a sign, not a magnitude: numeric contrast weights are never recorded, and a contrast whose magnitudes matter keeps them in `Analysis.definition`. There is no value for a zero weight either -- a level the contrast did not weight has no `Cell` at all.
Only `positive` and `negative` are directional. A cell can record no sign three ways -- `undirected`, `held`, or `extraction_status: not_reported` -- and choosing between them is the decision rule in extraction-readme.md §2.
Direction.title: Direction

EEG.description: A scalp EEG acquisition. Its own attributes are the ones that materially distinguish recordings used in source-localized coordinate or image-based meta-analyses.

acquisition_duration_seconds.description: Total usable acquisition or recording duration in seconds. Useful for filtering studies by the amount of data contributing to an analysis, especially resting-state and continuous recordings.

acquisition_type.description: The concrete subclass this record instantiates. Derived by the mapper from the modality value's `instantiates`, never extracted.

brain_coverage.description:
How much of the brain the acquired volume contained. This is the extent the SCANNER sampled, and it is a third axis distinct from the two the schema already carries: `Analysis.spatial_scope` is what the analysis tested, and `InferenceSettings.correction_scope` with `search_volume` is where multiple comparisons were controlled. A voxelwise analysis over a volume that clipped the cerebellum is `whole_brain` in scope and `partial` here, and an ROI analysis of a whole-head acquisition is the reverse. Never infer this from either of those.
It describes the volume behind the REPORTED results. A scan that clipped a structure in participants who were then excluded is `whole_brain`, because the analysed volume was not clipped; calling it `partial` would say the opposite of what the results rest on.
A field of view or slice prescription in millimetres is not by itself a statement of coverage. Where only the geometry is given, the value is an inference and `value_source` records it as one. Which structure a partial volume missed is not a field of its own -- the evidence span carries that detail.

device.description: The scanner, amplifier, or recording system this acquisition was made on, by identifier. Acquisitions made on one machine reference one record; a second record asserts the study used a second machine.

eeg_channel_count.description: Number of simultaneously recorded EEG channels.

eeg_placement_scheme.description: Electrode placement system, such as the 10-20 or 10-10 system.

eeg_reference.description: Reference scheme and location used for the raw recording.

modality.description:
Imaging or recording modality. A value in the Modality vocabulary also names the class holding this acquisition's modality-specific parameters, through that value's `instantiates`.
Open vocabulary: write the source's own wording in the field when nothing here fits, because the value is required and a closed range would discard the whole acquisition over one unrecognised word. Only a vocabulary value carries an `instantiates`, so an acquisition outside it resolves to the base class until normalization maps the wording back on -- which is why `acquisition_type` is derived rather than extracted, and why an unmapped modality is worth reporting.

recording_type.description: Recording organization, such as continuous, discontinuous, or epoched.

sampling_frequency_hz.description: Sampling frequency of the recording in hertz.

EEG.title: EEG

EdgeDirectionality.description:
Whether a connectivity edge is genuinely directed. Only directed models such as DCM and Granger causality qualify; a seed-to-voxel PPI or correlation is undirected, and its sign travels with the edge rather than implying a direction.
The one vocabulary nothing reads off the page: `ConnectivityEdge.directionality` is derived from `ConnectivityDetails.connectivity_method`, since the method decides it and no wording can override it.
EdgeDirectionality.title: EdgeDirectionality

Effect.description:
The inferential quantity tested about a map: what was compared, whether the comparison is a mediated path, and what statistic tested it. Estimation facts -- model family, estimator, stage, software -- belong to the ModelEstimation that produced the map.
The comparison is `cells`: one entry per level of a model term that entered the contrast, each with the side it sat on. Three things a reader might expect to find here are read off that instead:
- **what the contrast was adjusted for** -- the terms of the `ModelEstimation`, plus those
  of the stages it reaches through `inputs_from`, minus the terms these cells name.
- **what the map was tested against** -- a modelled reference is that condition's level
  with a `negative` cell; the unmodelled implicit baseline, or zero, is the absence of a
  second cell; a decoding metric's reference is `PerformanceMetric.reference_value`.

cells.description:
What this contrast compared: one entry per level of a model term that entered it, each with the side it sat on. The only place direction lives.
Every cell names its term, so the axis of a comparison is explicit. Two cells naming one term compare levels within that factor; cells naming different terms compare across them. A condition contrast, a cohort comparison, a pre-post change, a crossover comparison of arms and a region-by-condition dissociation all take this one form, and what distinguishes them is what the named term's levels range over, which `FactorLevel` states on the model.
Required and non-empty. A one-sample test is one signed cell: a lone `positive` cell tests that coefficient against zero, which is what the unmodelled implicit baseline is, and the sign distinguishes activation from deactivation. A map with no inferential test at all is not an Analysis.

kind.description:
What kind of test these cells describe, stated as well as encoded.
Redundant on purpose: the kind follows entirely from the cells by the ordered steps of extraction-readme.md §3, so a `kind` that disagrees with the cells beside it is a record contradicting itself. Neither half is authoritative -- a stated `contrast` over cells that derive `simple_effect` may be cells missing their second level, or a kind read off the analysis's title rather than its test. The pair says a reader should look, which is more than either half says alone.
The disagreement it most often catches is a decoding result encoded as a comparison: accuracy above chance is one signed cell and a `simple_effect` (§5.9), while two directionless cells derive `contrast` with its direction lost.

mediation.description: The mediation model this effect's quantity is a path through. Present only for a mediation analysis and absent otherwise, so an effect carries either a complete Mediation or none.

statistic.description: The statistic this effect was tested with, and its degrees of freedom. Not the value of the statistic at any location -- peak magnitudes belong to the reported coordinates.

Effect.title: Effect

EffectKind.description:
What kind of test an effect's cells describe. The range of `Effect.kind`, and also the output of deriving the same thing from the cells -- the two are compared, and a disagreement is a record contradicting itself.
This once had no slot at all, on the reasoning that the kind follows entirely from the cells and storing it would put one fact in two places. It does put it in two places, and that turned out to be the reason to store it: a cell pattern that derives nothing, or derives something other than what the analysis is, was invisible while the record stated the shape only once. There is no free-text branch: a cell pattern yields one of these labels or none, and a pattern yielding none is a record whose cells do not describe a test. The derivation is stated once, in extraction-readme.md §3.
EffectKind.title: EffectKind

EffectPath.description:
The path through a mediation model represented by an effect's map. Without it, an indirect-effect map is structurally identical to a plain regression on the same predictor, and a synthesis would pool the two.
No `not_applicable` value is needed: an effect outside a mediated path has no `Mediation` object or slot to fill.
EffectPath.title: EffectPath

nirs_placement_scheme.description: Standard placement system or listed optode positions, such as 10-20, Cz, or Pz.

nirs_system_type.description: Instrument principle, such as continuous-wave, frequency-domain, or time-domain NIRS.

FactorLevel.description:
One level of a categorical model term and the entities that carry it. The ModelTerm records which design cell a cohort or condition occupies because that placement belongs to the design, not to a contrast drawn from it.
The five entity slots are what make the entity view of a contrast recoverable: an Effect's cells name levels, and joining those levels here says which cohorts, conditions, occasions, arms or regions were compared. A factor normally ranges over one of the five -- conditions for a task factor, cohorts for a participant factor, occasions for a time factor, arms for a treatment factor, regions for one comparing places in the brain -- so the others stay empty; a level realized by a crossing, such as a drug given at follow-up, fills more than one.
A factor whose levels are not entities of the study at all -- hemispheres, tasks, frequency bands, acquisition sessions -- leaves all five empty and is carried by `level` alone. Such a factor is complete, and takes `Cell`s like any other.

arms.description: The arms carrying this level, by identifier. A factor whose levels are drug and placebo, or active and sham, ranges over arms. In a parallel trial each level is both an arm and a cohort and both slots are filled; in a crossover one cohort receives every arm, so `arms` alone distinguishes the levels and filling only `groups` loses the allocation.

conditions.description: The conditions carrying this level, by identifier.

groups.description: The participant cohorts carrying this level, by identifier.

level.description: The level's label, as the source words it. Unique within its term: a level appearing twice is one level recorded twice.

order.description:
Position of this level in the factor's sequence, counting from 1, for a factor whose levels are ordered. It carries an ordering `Effect.cells` cannot: a contrast signs only its extremes and omits what lies between, so without this 1-back, 2-back and 3-back are an unordered set.
Populate it whenever the levels have an order the source states or plainly implies -- a dose series, a load or difficulty series, an ordinal severity grading. Leave it unset for a nominal factor, where imposing an order would assert a structure the design does not have. Timepoint.order is the same device for occasions.

regions.description: The brain regions carrying this level, by identifier, for a factor comparing places. A three-region factor is one `ModelTerm` with three levels, one region on each.

timepoints.description: The occasions carrying this level, by identifier. A factor whose levels are baseline, week 6 or follow-up ranges over occasions and fills this: left empty, the level stands on its label alone and no query can tell which scan preceded the intervention.

FactorLevel.title: FactorLevel

FunctionalForm.description: Shape of a term's relationship to the measure. A squared term with a negative coefficient is an inverted-U relationship, not a negative association, so non-linear and transformed terms must not be reported as linear. Open vocabulary: write the source's own wording in the field when nothing here fits.
FunctionalForm.title: FunctionalForm

Group.description: An aggregate participant group and its reported demographics.

acquired_count.description: Number for whom data were acquired or who were scanned.

age_maximum.description: Oldest age reported for the group.

age_mean.description: Mean participant age in the unit given by age_unit.

age_median.description: Median participant age for the group.

age_minimum.description: Youngest age reported for the group.

age_standard_deviation.description: Standard deviation of participant age in the unit given by age_unit.

age_unit.description: Unit used for age summaries, normally years but potentially months, weeks, or gestational weeks.

age_unit_normalized.description:
`age_unit` folded onto a fixed set. **Derived, not extracted**: `pondie.normalization.age_unit` sets it from the source's own wording, which is kept in `age_unit`.
Without it the age fields are not comparable across studies: `6` under "months" and `6` under "years" are the same number, and a filter on age reads every neonatal and infant cohort wrong. `UNKNOWN` where the wording does not say -- not `years`, because assuming the common case is what makes that error silent.

approached_count.description: Number of prospective participants approached for this group.

arm.description: The arm this cohort was allocated to. Set it whenever a cohort was allocated to one, which is the parallel-group case: every participant of this cohort received this arm and no other. A crossover study allocates nobody to one arm, so its cohorts leave this empty and an arm reaches an analysis only as a level of a model term, through `FactorLevel.arms`. Distinct from `medication_status`, which is the on/off state during acquisition rather than the allocation.

clinical_characteristics.description: Disease duration, severity, treatment status, or other clinically relevant summaries.

consented_count.description: Number who consented or assented to participate.

description.description: Narrative definition of the group and its role in the study.

diagnostic_instrument.description: The study assessment that established this group's defining condition -- the `medical_condition` entries, or for a healthy group its confirmed absence. Naming one here claims it classified this cohort, which is narrower than having been administered to it: an interview screening a comorbidity the group is not defined by, or grading the severity of a diagnosis made elsewhere, is recorded in `assessments` and pointed at from nowhere. Groups defined by enrollment or history rather than by an assessment -- a treatment programme's patients, self-reported users -- name nothing, as do sources reporting a diagnostic system but never the instrument applying it. Every entry must also appear in the study's `assessments`.

diagnostic_system.description: Classification system and edition under which this group's `medical_condition` was diagnosed, such as DSM-5 or ICD-10. An edition that appears only inside an instrument's title does not establish it: "SCID for DSM-IV Axis II Disorders", administered to screen comorbidities, says nothing about the system used to diagnose the condition that defines the group.

education_summary.description: Aggregate education level and the measurement or coding system used.

enrolled_count.description: Number enrolled after screening and before acquisition.

ethnicity_distribution.description: Aggregate ethnic distribution using the study-reported category labels.

excluded_count.description: Number excluded after consent, enrollment, acquisition, and quality control.

exclusion_criteria.description: Screening, imaging-safety, clinical, behavioral, or quality-control criteria causing exclusion.

gender_distribution.description: Aggregate self-described gender distribution, kept separate from phenotypic sex. Use one entry per reported category.

handedness_distribution.description: Aggregate handedness distribution. Use one entry per reported category, such as right-handed, left-handed, or ambidextrous.

inclusion_criteria.description: Eligibility requirements that a participant had to satisfy for membership in this group.

is_healthy.description:
Whether this cohort is free of medical, neurological and psychiatric conditions. **Derived, not extracted**: code sets it from `medical_condition`, so it cannot disagree with it.
True when the group records no condition, or records only an assertion of absence ("no neurological or psychiatric disorder", "healthy controls"). False when any entry is a condition. Unset when `medical_condition` was never extracted -- that is not a healthy cohort, it is an unread one.
Derived rather than asked because the source's own wording does not settle it: the addiction and obesity literature says "healthy" to mean free of comorbidity.

medical_condition.description: Medical, neurological, psychiatric, developmental, or physiological condition(s) defining or characterizing the group. List the primary diagnosis and all comorbidities.

medication_status.description: Whether the cohort was medicated, unmedicated, drug-naive, or withdrawn, and the on/off medication state during acquisition or testing. The state, not the agents: which drugs they were taking is `medications`.

medications.description: The drugs or other agents this cohort was taking, as the source names them, one agent per entry. Names only.

name.description: Study-local group label, for example healthy controls or patients with Parkinson disease.

other_characteristics.description:
Cohort traits that are true but not selective: the entries moved out of `population_characteristics` because every plausible cohort could carry them. "normal weight", "typically developing", "right-handed", "normal or corrected-to-normal vision", "no history of neurological illness", "MRI compatible", "native English speakers" are the recurring forms.
**Derived, not extracted.** `pondie.normalization.population_characteristics` partitions the extracted list and code writes this side of it, so the slot is never put to a model. It exists because the alternative to moving these values is dropping them, which loses a cohort detail a reader auditing the study wants to see.
The partition is by selectivity, not by truth. A value here is not wrong; it is a value no query can usefully filter on, which is the only reason it cannot share a field with the trait a study chose its cohort for.
Asymmetric where the literature is: "right-handed" is normative and "left-handed" or "mixed-handed" is selective, because a study recruiting left-handers recruited for that. Likewise a negated *condition* is normative ("no psychiatric history") and a negated *exposure* is not ("no history of smoking" defines the control arm of a smoking study).

population_characteristics.description:
How this cohort **deviates from the typical**, where no other field covers it: habitual exposure (heavy caffeine use, social drinkers, smoking status), training or expertise (athletes, musicians, bilinguals, gamers), occupation or social role (veterans, undergraduates, shift workers), lifestyle (sedentary, vegetarian, meditation practitioners), and body habitus where it is atypical (obese, overweight, underweight).
Deviation is the test, and it is what makes this field worth querying. A study selects its cohort for something; that something is what belongs here. The unremarkable does not: "normal weight", "healthy weight", "typically developing", "right-handed", "no hearing loss" and an ordinary age range describe a cohort that was not selected for anything, and recording them fills the field with the absence of information. If every plausible cohort could carry the value, leave it out.
**Every other Group slot takes priority.** Nothing here that belongs in `age_mean`, `age_minimum`, `age_maximum`, `age_median`, `sex_distribution`, `gender_distribution`, `handedness_distribution`, `race_distribution`, `ethnicity_distribution`, `education_summary`, `socioeconomic_status_summary`, `medications`, `medication_status`, `recruitment_method`, `species`, `inclusion_criteria`, `exclusion_criteria` or `medical_condition`. "All Caucasian" is `race_distribution`; "children aged 8-11" is `age_minimum` and `age_maximum`; "five participants were female" is `sex_distribution`.
Not a diagnosis either. Where a trait is also the cohort's condition -- alcohol dependence, obesity as a diagnosed disease -- `medical_condition` takes it alone, which is where a clinician would look.
What was screened out is not a characteristic. "Excluding caffeine" in an exclusion list says nothing about caffeine use in the cohort.

race_distribution.description: Aggregate racial distribution using the study-reported category labels.

recruitment_dates.description: Free-text recruitment period when the source does not support a precise normalized date range; examples include January 2021 to June 2022, 2018-2020, or autumn 2023.

recruitment_method.description: How, where, and from what setting participants were recruited.

sample_overlap_count.description: How many of this group were in that prior report, when the source says so. It is the difference between two papers being one sample and their sharing part of one, which is the difference between dropping a study and down-weighting it.

sample_source.description:
Where this group's participants came from. `recruited` when they were enrolled for this study and no other source is stated; `public_dataset` when they were drawn from a named public or consortium dataset; `previously_reported` when the same or an overlapping sample was already reported in another publication.
On the group and not the study, because overlap is routinely partial: a study may scan a fresh patient group against controls taken from an existing dataset, and a study-level flag cannot say which. `Study.external_datasets` remains the place for a named dataset the study as a whole used.
A protocol, preprocessing pipeline or analysis "described previously" is a shared METHOD and leaves this `recruited`; so does comparing findings to earlier literature in the discussion. Only a statement that these same people were scanned, studied or reported before counts, and a source that means it normally says so in one sentence.
`recruited` is an assertion and not the absence of one. A meta-analysis excluding overlapping samples has to distinguish a study that recruited freshly from one nobody checked, and an unfilled field cannot.

sample_source_reference.description: The dataset name, or the prior publication as the source cites it: an author-year citation, a bracketed reference number, or a trial registration number, copied as written. Without it the overlap is known but not actionable -- deciding whether two papers are one independent sample needs the identity of the other one.

sex_distribution.description: Aggregate phenotypic sex distribution. Use one entry per reported category, with the study's category label and a count and/or percentage. A cohort described wholly as one sex reports its distribution without ever printing a breakdown: "22 male smokers", "young women (n = 8)" and "ten male patients" are each one entry whose count is the whole group, plus a second entry for the absent sex with a count of zero. Read a demographics table row ("N female | 5") exactly as you would read the same fact in a sentence.

socioeconomic_status_summary.description: Aggregate socioeconomic status and the instrument or proxy used to measure it.

InferenceSettings.description:
One thresholding and correction procedure. This is the canonical storage home for thresholding, correction, and cluster-inference metadata. The test statistic itself belongs to the tested effect and lives in Effect.statistic.
One record may be referenced by several Analyses, so every field must hold for all of them; an analysis thresholded or corrected differently takes its own record. The test is mechanical: two analyses share a record when the threshold, its type, the correction method, the scope corrected over and the alpha are all the same. A paper that states one correction scheme in Methods and applies it throughout has one record.
Inference attaches to the analysis, not to the fit: one model estimated once is often thresholded several ways -- an ROI test Bonferroni-corrected over four regions and a searchlight over the same fit corrected by FDR. See storage-schema-design-notes.md for the reasoning behind this shape.

alpha_level.description: Family-wise, false-discovery, or nominal alpha threshold when reported.

cluster_extent_threshold.description: Minimum surviving cluster extent in voxels, vertices, or the unit stated in the source.

clusterwise_threshold_value.description: Numeric cluster-level threshold for retaining clusters.

correction_regions.description:
The regions correction was restricted to -- what `correction_scope: roi` names, as `Analysis.regions` names what `spatial_scope: roi` restricts the search space to. Empty for a whole-brain correction.
Not the analysis's search space. Naming the correction mask on the analysis instead says the model was fitted within it, which is a different claim about what the paper did.

correction_scope.description:
Whether the multiple-comparison correction searched the whole acquired volume or was restricted to regions. The correction's own domain, not the analysis's: a whole-brain voxelwise model whose significance was corrected inside an anatomical mask has `Analysis.spatial_scope: whole_brain` and `correction_scope: roi`, and the two differing is the ordinary case rather than a contradiction.
A domain the enum cannot name is written here as free text. An inference level such as "cluster level" is not a scope and belongs in `inference_level`.

height_threshold_type.description: Meaning of height_threshold_value, such as p, q, t, z, or F.

height_threshold_value.description:
The threshold applied to each element's statistic, before correction and before any cluster-level test. Papers name it for whichever of its two jobs they are describing -- the *voxelwise* (or vertexwise) threshold when elements are tested individually, the *cluster-forming* threshold when surviving elements are grouped into clusters -- and it is one number either way, applied once to the map. Record it once here, whichever word the source uses.
Not the cluster-level threshold: `clusterwise_threshold_value` is the p or q a whole cluster had to beat, and `cluster_extent_threshold` the size it had to reach. A paper reporting "p < 0.001 uncorrected, cluster-level p < 0.05 FWE" states this field and `clusterwise_threshold_value`, not this field twice.

id.description: Stable identifier used by Analysis foreign-key references.

inference_level.description: Level at which inference is made, such as voxel, vertex, cluster, region, network or other.

multiple_comparison_method.description: Correction method, such as FWE, FDR, Bonferroni, permutation, Monte Carlo, or none.

neighborhood_definition.description: Voxel or vertex adjacency or connectivity rule used for cluster formation.

number_of_tests.description: Number of statistical tests considered by the multiple-comparison procedure.

permutation_count.description: Number of permutations, randomizations, or simulations used for inference.

search_volume.description: Reported search volume, mask size, or number of vertices or voxels used for inference.

tfce_parameters.description: TFCE parameters such as height and extent exponents when reported.

tfce_used.description: Whether threshold-free cluster enhancement was used.

InferenceSettings.title: InferenceSettings

InferenceTarget.description: What the connectivity analysis drew inference about. Open vocabulary: write the source's own wording in the field when nothing here fits.

LatentDecompositionDetails.description:
Payload for an analysis whose map is one component or latent variable of a decomposition -- ICA, PCA, NMF, PLS, CCA, and the multimodal fusion methods. Covers a component whose map or loading was *tested*: compared between cohorts, correlated with behaviour, or otherwise given an inferential result. A component map presented descriptively with no test is not an Analysis, so it takes no record here. Being representable here does not imply eligibility for coordinate-based meta-analysis.
One analysis reports one component: a second latent variable or component from the same decomposition is a second Analysis.
One invariant LinkML does not express, so the structural validator carries it: `crossblock_covariance_percent` is meaningless when `second_block` is `[none]`, there being no second block for the covariance to cross. `variance_explained_percent` is permitted either way, since a two-block decomposition may still report how much of the brain block its component captures.

component_id.description: Identifier of the component or latent variable within the decomposition, as reported -- commonly an index such as `IC12` or `LV1`. Required because without it two analyses from one decomposition are indistinguishable.

component_label.description: The source's name for the component, such as a network label, or for what a latent variable captures.

crossblock_covariance_percent.description: Percentage of crossblock covariance this latent variable accounts for, as reported. The nearest thing a two-block decomposition has to an effect size, and what a paper uses to justify reporting one latent variable and not another. Unset when `second_block` is `[none]`, there being no second block to cross.

details_type.description: The concrete details subclass carried by this payload. Populated from the class itself, not extracted.

dimensionality_selection_method.description: How the number of components was chosen, as reported -- minimum description length, a variance-retained cutoff, a scree criterion, permutation on the singular values, or a fixed a priori number.

map_quantity.description: What the values of the reported map represent -- a loading, a weight, a PLS salience, a standardized score.

method.description: The algorithm that produced the components, which decides what their values and signs mean.

polarity_semantics.description: Whether the sign of the reported map carries meaning. A latent variable's sign is arbitrary up to a flip, and so is an independent component's, so a paper must say what positive means before a direction can be pooled.

salience_threshold.description: The criterion deciding which elements count as reliable contributors, as reported -- conventionally a bootstrap ratio cutoff such as "|BSR| > 3.0", or a standardized cutoff such as "|Z| > 3.5". Not `InferenceSettings`: a bootstrap ratio is a stability measure and not a test statistic, so reading it as a voxelwise threshold would misstate the inference.

second_block.description:
What the brain block was decomposed against, one value per additional block, and the primary filter on this payload. `[none]` for a decomposition of the brain data alone, which is a positive assertion rather than an empty slot.
Multivalued because papers cross more than two blocks: a three-modality mCCA+jICA carries `other_imaging_modality` twice, and a design-plus-behaviour PLS carries `[design, behavioral]`. Name the blocks, never their number.

second_block_assessments.description: The measures forming a behavioural or clinical block, by identifier, when they are `Assessment` records of this study. Empty when the second block is the design, another imaging modality, or anything else that is not an assessment -- those are named in `second_block_detail`.

second_block_detail.description: What each non-assessment block held, in the source's words: the seed regions of a seed decomposition, the modalities of a fusion ("ALFF, FA, grey matter"), the genotype array of a parallel ICA ("367 SNPs"). Free text because the range of things that form a second block is open, and a SNP array is neither an `Assessment` nor an `Acquisition` of this study.

selection_criterion.description: How this component was selected for reporting.

total_components.description: Number of components or latent variables the decomposition produced.

variance_explained_percent.description: Percentage of the brain block's variance this component accounts for, as reported. Not interchangeable with `crossblock_covariance_percent`: one is variance within a block and the other covariance between blocks, and averaging across the two would combine incomparable quantities.

MassUnivariateDetails.description:
Payload for a voxelwise, vertexwise, or ROI-wise GLM, mixed-effects model, ANOVA, ANCOVA, or robust regression -- the default family. It adds no fields: what was tested is in Effect and how it was estimated is in ModelEstimation.
A voxelwise **mediation** analysis is one of these. Each path it reports is estimated by regression, so the fit is mass-univariate and what makes the map a mediation is `Effect.mediation` -- the path tested, and the term it runs through. Reaching for OtherAnalysisDetails because the word "mediation" has no first-class payload leaves `Effect.mediation` empty, and an indirect-effect map with no path recorded is indistinguishable from a plain regression on the same predictor.

Measure.description:
The scientific quantity of the map, independent of the statistic used to test it. When a paper alternates terms for the same map -- grey matter concentration in Methods and volume in Results -- take the Methods term for type and keep both wordings in source_label.
One record may be referenced by several Analyses, so every field must hold for all of them; an analysis of a different quantity takes its own record. The test is mechanical: two analyses share a record when `family`, `type`, `specific_metric` and `unit` all match. A study measures one or two quantities and tests them many ways, so sharing is the common case -- eight analyses of one connectivity measure are one record, not eight.
Not a property of the thresholding scheme: one correction scheme routinely covers several measures, and one measure is often tested under several schemes. See storage-schema-design-notes.md for the reasoning behind this shape.

family.description: Broad imaging or signal family, for coarse filtering.

id.description: Stable identifier used by Analysis foreign-key references.

source_label.description: The paper's own term for the measure. Unset only when the source does not identify the measure.

specific_metric.description: Named metric when type is intentionally broad, such as fractional anisotropy, ALFF, fALFF, or a specific tracer binding potential.

unit.description: The unit the measure is reported in, when the source gives one and it carries information -- mm for a thickness, mL for a volume. Omitted for a unitless quantity such as a correlation or a normalized index.

Activation and deactivation are directions rather than measure types; both are bold_response and the directional roles carry the direction. Gray-matter density is not collapsed into volume. A paper that does not identify the measure leaves the slot `extraction_status: not_reported`. Open vocabulary: write the source's own wording in the field when nothing here fits.

path.description: The path through the mediation model represented by this effect's map. An effect that is not a mediated path has no Mediation, so there is no `not_applicable` case.

ModelEstimation.description:
How a model was specified in software and estimated: its terms, the family, the source's wording for it, the estimator, the stage, the software, the pipeline that produced the data it was fitted to, and the spatial element it was fitted over. One record may be referenced by several Analyses, so every field must hold for all of them; an analysis specified or estimated differently takes its own record. **The data a model was fitted to is part of its specification**.
One record is one estimation stage. Neuroimaging splits a model across stages for tractability, and `inputs_from` is what puts it back together: a stage's terms are its own plus those of the stages it consumed, so the split costs the record nothing while each stage keeps its own family, estimator, software and basis.

estimator.description: Estimation method, such as OLS, WLS, maximum likelihood, restricted maximum likelihood, permutation, or Bayesian estimation.

hrf_model.description: The haemodynamic response basis the design matrix was built with: a canonical HRF, a canonical plus temporal or dispersion derivatives, an FIR or gamma basis, or a named alternative. Unset for a measure that models no timeseries -- morphometry, diffusion, static PET.

id.description: Stable identifier used by Analysis foreign-key references.

inputs_from.description:
The models whose fitted output this model was estimated on: the first-level GLM whose contrast images a group model takes as its data, the subject-level fit an ROI ANOVA summarises. The stage graph, recorded only where the source states it.
**A model's terms are its own plus, transitively, those of the models named here.** That combined list is what `terms` would be had the analysis been fitted in one step.
Leave it empty when the source describes one design matrix, and when it describes the lower stage too thinly to constitute a model. Empty is not a claim that no lower stage existed; it is the absence of a statement about one, exactly as an unrecorded term is.
Must be acyclic, no model may reach itself.

model_family.description: Normalized statistical model family, which is the queryable form. Required, so a paper that never says still carries the slot, as `extraction_status: not_reported`. A method the vocabulary cannot name -- ICA, representational similarity, a decoder -- is written here as free text; the Analysis.details subclass also identifies the method.

model_settings.description: Essential estimator, variance, autocorrelation, covariance, regularization, and software-specific settings.

model_type.description: The source's own wording for the model, minimally cleaned, such as mass- univariate GLM, meta-analysis, multivariate, predictive model, ICA, or representational similarity analysis.

preprocessing.description:
The pipelines that produced the data this model was fitted to. Every Analysis referencing this record came through them, so a model fitted to differently prepared data -- unsmoothed images for a classifier, smoothed ones for a mass-univariate fit -- takes its own record rather than sharing one.
More than one entry when the fit consumed more than one kind of image: a multimodal regression of perfusion on grey-matter volume was fitted to the output of both pipelines, and naming either alone says the other's smoothing and normalisation did not touch the map.

software.description: Statistical software name, version, and relevant implementation details.

spatial_unit.description:
The element this model was fitted over. Distinct from the Analysis's `spatial_scope`, which gives the extent rather than the element: a whole-brain model can be voxelwise or vertexwise, and a model over an ROI can average the region or test its parcels. Record it rather than inferring it from `coordinate_space`.
A model fitted over a different element is a different model, so a voxelwise GLM and an ROI-mean ANOVA of the same design take two records: no contrast of one can be read off the other's fit.

stage.description:
Stage of analysis, in the source's terms: run, session, subject and group are the usual words, and any other the source uses is storable as written. Deliberately left open -- no vocabulary fits every design, and nothing derives anything from it.
A label, not an ordering. Only `inputs_from` records which stage fed another: two records labelled `group` say nothing about their relationship, and these strings never imply a chain.

terms.description:
The terms **this stage** was specified with -- the columns of its design matrix, in the general sense that covers a GLM's regressors and the predictors of any other family. Stated once here however many contrasts are taken from them, and never restated on a stage above: the terms of a lower stage are reached through `inputs_from`.
Record every term the source states, including ones no reported contrast tests, and including ones mentioned only in passing: "controlling for age and sex" is a statement about the design matrix. This list, together with the lists reached through `inputs_from`, is **the adjustment set of every contrast taken from this model** -- each contrast's is that combined list minus the terms its cells name -- so a term omitted from every stage reads as one the model did not adjust for. Where the list is incomplete, the slot's extraction_status is what says so.
May be empty, and legitimately is for a stage that fits only an intercept: a one-sample group test over first-level contrast images has no column of its own. Do not invent an intercept term to fill it.
Analyses whose design matrices differ take their own records rather than sharing one.
